lastCompletedGameRecap.recapHeadline: Seahawks beat Raiders 21-13 as Drew Lock throws for 2 TDs and Seattle sacks Fernando Mendoza 6 times
lastCompletedGameRecap.recapLeadExcerpt: LAS VEGAS -- — The lead-up to Sunday's Seattle-Las Vegas matchup was almost all about Fernando Mendoza , at last receiving his first start as the Raiders' quarterback.  But it was Drew Lock , the Seahawks' journeyman backup, who shined.  Lock passed for 240 yards and two touchdowns, including a game-breaking 71-yard scoring toss to Jaxon Smith-Njigba , and Seattle beat Las Vegas 21-13 to spoil Mendoza's debut.  The defending Super Bowl champion but injury-riddled Seahawks (6-4), playing their first regular-season game at Allegiant Stadium, have won three of four entering their bye week. The top pick in this year's draft, elevated after Kirk Cousins was traded Tuesday to Minnesota, looked sharp early in leading the Raiders to 10 points on their first two drives.
lastCompletedGameRecap.inGameInjuryNotes: Injuries Seahawks: Their banged-up offensive line suffered another setback when RT Abraham Lucas was injured in the second quarter. LG Quenton Nelson (knee) and LT Charles Cross (ankle) were inactive. ... RB George Holani (knee) went out in the first quarter.
lastCompletedGameRecap.upNextNotes: Up next Seahawks: At San Francisco on Nov. 29. Raiders: At Denver next Sunday.

injuryReport.name: Austen Pleasants
injuryReport.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
factors: Season-ending Injured Reserve — ineligible to return this season
injuryReport.beatComment: Pleasants opened the regular season on injured reserve due to a knee injury that he sustained in a preseason game against the Chargers in late August. He was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, and he would need to be activated from injured reserve in order to be available for Sunday's game against the Seahawks. With Colton McKivitz (ankle) out for the rest of the season, Pleasants would be a candidate to start at right tackle once he's removed from IR.

injuryReport.name: Jordan Watkins
injuryReport.beatComment: Watkins may have injured his groin during the 49ers' 35-10 win over the Vikings in Week 11, when he hauled in his lone target for 19 yards while playing 28 snaps on offense. His practice participation over the next two days will shed light on his status heading into Sunday's NFC West tilt against the Seahawks. If Watkins cannot play in Week 12, then Keenan Allen, Jacob Cowing and Demarcus Robinson would all be in line for larger roles on offense.

injuryReport.name: Brock Purdy
injuryReport.beatComment: Purdy put on a master class during this past Sunday's 35-10 win against the Vikings in Mexico City, completing 21 of 26 passes for 255 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. Now with a health concern in tow, his status will be monitored closely to get a sense of his odds to suit up Sunday against the Seahawks. Mac Jones is waiting in the wings in the event Purdy isn't able to play in Week 12.

injuryReport.name: Mike Evans
factors: Did Not Participate (DNP) on Wednesday (veteran maintenance profile, awaiting Thursday workload)
injuryReport.beatComment: After a three-game (and four-week) absence due to right Achilles tendinitis, Evans returned to action during Sunday's win against the Vikings in Mexico City, recording a 43 percent offensive snap share and gathering in six of seven targets for 109 yards and one touchdown. The 49ers likely are managing Evans' workload to begin Week 12 prep, but his status nonetheless will be monitored in advance of Sunday's contest against the Seahawks.

injuryReport.name: Dre Greenlaw
factors: Wednesday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 81%
injuryReport.beatComment: Greenlaw was not cleared by medical staff to play against the Vikings in Week 11 due to a neck issue. He's opened Week 12 prep with a limited practice, and a full session over the next two days would likely be enough for him to avoid an injury designation ahead of Sunday's game against the Seahawks.

injuryReport.name: Deommodore Lenoir
factors: Wednesday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 92%
injuryReport.beatComment: Lenoir has been playing through a foot injury since Week 9 against the Raiders, so it's not surprising to see his practice reps limited Wednesday. Unless he suffers a setback, Lenoir should be available for Sunday's NFC West tilt against the Seahawks.

injuryReport.name: Keenan Allen
factors: Habitual Veteran Rest prior (Keenan Allen maintenance schedule)
injuryReport.beatComment: Sunday marked Allen's first time working with Mike Evans, the 49ers' top wide receiver, and the latter dominated the attention of QB Brock Purdy, posting a 6-109-1 line on seven targets in his first game action since Week 6. If Evans' Achilles issue flares up at any point, Allen may be thrust into WR1 duties, which could yield more consistent results as he becomes more acclimated to head coach Kyle Shanahan's offense. For now, though, Allen will play a distant second to Evans for as long as the latter is healthy and available.

irReserve.name: Colton McKivitz
irReserve.byeWeekNote: Season-ending IR — ineligible to return in 2026
factors: On Injured Reserve — 21-day practice window not yet opened
irReserve.beatComment: McKivitz was diagnosed with a fractured and dislocated ankle that he sustained in the 49ers' Week 11 win over the Vikings. He's expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, and Vederian Lowe is expected to take over as the starter at right tackle in McKivitz's absence.

irReserve.name: Sam Okuayinonu
factors: On Injured Reserve — 21-day practice window not yet opened
irReserve.beatComment: Okuayinonu suffered a broken foot in practice ahead of Week 1 and required surgery. He appears to be making progress and could return at some point before the end of the regular season. The 28-year-old appeared in 15 regular-season games last season, and made 12 starts and recorded 23 tackles (16 solo), including 3.0 sacks, and a forced fumble.

irReserve.name: De'Zhaun Stribling
factors: On Injured Reserve — 21-day practice window not yet opened
irReserve.beatComment: Stribling was diagnosed with a deltoid sprain of his left ankle after getting injured in the 49ers' Week 1 win over the Rams in Australia and underwent surgery Sept. 16. The 23-year-old was handed an estimated recovery timeline of about 10 weeks, leaving the 49ers optimistic that he would be ready to play at some point in December. While Shanahan indicated that Stribling's timeline doesn't appear to have changed, the young wideout will need to get back on the practice field before the 49ers can hone in on a more precise target date for him to resume playing. Given the haziness of his return date along with the fact that he could face limitations with his snaps once activated, Stribling likely isn't worth holding in redraft leagues at this point in the season.

coachingMatchup.headline: Mike Macdonald & DC Aden Durde vs. HC Kyle Shanahan, OC Klay Kubiak & DC Raheem Morris (Road Test)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting Seattle Seahawks's staff (Mike Macdonald, OC Brian Fleury, DC Aden Durde) against San Francisco 49ers (9-1)—testing both Seattle's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and coverage discipline.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Mike Macdonald and OC Brian Fleury pair condensed splits with pre-snap jet motion and orbit motion to stress San Francisco 49ers's single-high vs. two-high rotations—widening curl/flat defenders to attack the honey-hole between hook/curl linebackers and deep safeties on play-action choice/dagger concepts.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: Against San Francisco 49ers's pin-and-pull, counter, and duo runs targeting the A- and B-gaps, DC Aden Durde balances four-man pressure with disguised Quarters and Cover 6 split-safety rotations on early downs and in the red zone.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: Third-down conversion discipline and red-zone touchdown rate govern whether Seattle sustains multi-play scoring drives or yields momentum to San Francisco 49ers's pass rush and coverage disguises.
Tempo, Turnovers & Venue Leverage: Road Test situational play-calling, penalty margin, and turnover differential provide the clearest late-game swing factors for both coaching staffs.

keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: SEA: #17 Pass Off (218.5 yds) · #20 Off. Scoring (-1.20) | SF: #16 Pass Def (+1.78)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Drew Lock, AJ Barner & Jaxon Smith-Njigba attack the intermediate seams and middle-of-the-field leverage windows against San Francisco 49ers's #16 pass defense (+1.78). Winning early-down timing throws keeps Seattle's offense ahead of the chains and punishes disguised single-high rotations.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Drew Lock (#2) scanning 49ers's deep safeties at the snap—when LB Fred Warner widens to take away the crossers, the intermediate seam opens immediately for AJ Barner (#88).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Leonard Williams, Byron Murphy II & Jarran Reed vs. QB Mac Jones & G Connor Colby
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: SEA: #16 Def Sacks (2.3/gm) | SF: #16 Pass Protection (6.5%)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Leonard Williams, Byron Murphy II & Jarran Reed lead Seattle's #16 NFL pass rush (2.3/gm) against San Francisco 49ers's #16 pass-protection unit (6.5%). Collapsing the interior pocket without sending extra blitzers lets Seahawks keep seven defenders in coverage.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: On 3rd-and-6+, watch whether Leonard Williams (#99) draw chip help from 49ers's tight ends or backs—creating 1-on-1 rush lanes inside for Byron Murphy II (#91).

keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Ernest Jones IV, Devon Witherspoon & Julian Love anchor Seattle's #4 pass defense (-3.19) against WR Deebo Samuel Sr. and San Francisco 49ers's #6 passing attack (255.5 yds). Limiting explosive 20+ yard chunk plays forces 49ers into sustained red-zone drives.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Track Ernest Jones IV (#13) at the top of routes against WR Deebo Samuel Sr.: press-bail alignment with safety help over the top takes away QB Mac Jones's preferred isolation shots.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Zach Charbonnet & Brady Russell vs. 49ers Front Seven & LB Fred Warner

keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Zach Charbonnet & Brady Russell test San Francisco 49ers's #4 run defense (-1.79) with horizontal stretch and interior cutback lanes. Generating 4.5+ yards on first down unlocks play-action explosives and neutralizes 49ers's pass-rush packages.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether 49ers's linebackers over-pursue motion to the perimeter—opening decisive backside B-gap cutback lanes for Zach Charbonnet (#26).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Grey Zabel, Jalen Sundell & Charles Cross vs. DE Keion White & 49ers Simulated Pressures
